method: Actual current mediation handler; only model overridden for this process; one generation, no retry.

input.dispute: Utilities split evenly three ways when one person is home all day and the other two are not
input.yourSide: I work from home so I'm here with the heating on while they're both out. I get why they think even splits are simplest, but I'm also not the one who set the thermostat to 22 in November. I'd pay a bigger share of heating if we split internet and water evenly.
input.theirSide: They say an even split is the only thing that doesn't turn into a monthly argument, and that once you start metering one thing you end up metering everything. One of them also pointed out I use less water since I shower at the gym.

response.understanding: Utilities currently appear to be split equally three ways, though no explicit agreement is described. You work from home with the heating on, but being home does not establish how much extra heating costs you cause; the thermostat setting also matters. You would consider paying more for heating if internet and water stayed equal. That is an offer, not an obligation or an accepted deal. As you understand it, your housemates favor equal shares to avoid recurring arguments, and one acknowledges your lower water use. Those offsets matter when judging the whole arrangement. What remains unclear is whether anyone actually wants the split changed or whether you are questioning its fairness yourself.

way_forward.recommendation: First clarify whether anyone is requesting a change. If everyone prefers the existing split, there is no need to introduce usage accounting. If someone wants a change, discuss a simple heating-only adjustment alongside an agreed daytime thermostat setting, while explicitly deciding whether water and internet remain equal.
way_forward.reason: This addresses both the potential extra heating burden and your limited control over its cost, without treating your presence at home as proof that you owe more or ignoring your lower water use. Any revised split should be mutually accepted rather than inferred from your willingness to contribute.
supporting_actions: If considering an extra heating contribution, check whether heating costs can reasonably be separated from the rest of the bill before choosing an amount; avoid applying a surcharge to all utilities.

words_you_can_use.script: Are either of you asking to change the split, or would you rather keep it equal? I’m open to paying more toward heating if water and internet stay evenly split, but I’d also want us to agree on the daytime temperature—I didn’t choose 22 degrees. I’d prefer something simple rather than tracking everything.
